title: `st.data_editor` doesn’t return the input value unless you press Enter or click outside the editor
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Unlike `st.number_input`, `st.text_area`, and other widgets, `st.data_editor` only returns the input value after the user presses Enter or clicks outside the currently focused cell (excluding clicks on buttons).

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7868)

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st


def set_state(i: int, df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    st.session_state.stage = i
    st.session_state.df = df


if "stage" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.stage = 0

if st.session_state.stage == 0:
    st.write("Input your data")
    df = st.data_editor(pd.DataFrame({"col1": ["a", "b"], "col2": ["c", "d"]}))
    st.button(
        "Begin",
        on_click=set_state,
        args=[1, df],
    )

if st.session_state.stage == 1:
    st.write("Your data")
    st.dataframe(st.session_state.df)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click and edit a cell
2. Press the `Begin` button without clicking another area or pressing the Enter key.
3. Input value is not shown (input value is not returned from `st.data_editor`)

![Screen Recording 2023-12-22 at 2 02 09](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/45100960/0bd9f592-772c-440f-b06c-c73eee2e55c2)



### Expected Behavior

Input value is shown after clicking the button (input value is returned from `st.data_editor`).

### Current Behavior

Input value is not shown after clicking the button (input value is not returned from `st.data_editor`).

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:
  - 1.29.0
- Python version:
  - 3.11.6
- Operating System:
  - Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS
- Browser:
  - Google Chrome


### Additional Information

If this is an expected behavior, feel free to close this issue.

Hey [USER],
Input value is shown after clicking the button and also Enter key is not pressed.

[Screencast from 22-12-23 08:35:18 PM IST.webm](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/105560839/8e981800-fe3b-4bfa-a11e-ed8b0b734e69)

Hello [USER],
After receiving your response, I tried inputting the value and clicking the button several times, but sometimes the input value is shown, and sometimes it is not.
Therefore, this issue may be due to a race condition.

![Screen Recording 2023-12-23 at 1 24 53](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/45100960/4c8c2c00-7c28-48c7-bbbb-09b377ead7f0)

Hello [USER],
Now, I too tried inputting the value again and clicking the button, however sometimes the input value is shown, and it's not.
May be there is a need to create a new widget or parameters to solve this issue based on race condition.

I was able to reproduce the issue [here](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-7868). This does indeed look like a race condition. There are two reruns fired in a short interval, the rerun of the button click and the one from the data editor input change. The issue is a bit similar to this one: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7862

[USER] this might only be a real problem with button-like elements (or things like st.page_link), since I can't think of another element that a user could "switch" to which would "instantly" issue reruns. Is it possible for a button presses to "collect" all other rerun requests from elements on the page before they send their own rerun request?
[USER]  Yep, that is a good idea. Maybe even just adding a very short delay (e.g. 10ms) for sending out the button trigger event would solve that as well.

Funnily enough I ran into this very problem not 10 minutes after posting last night 😂.

A short delay could work, though I think that makes some assumptions about the execution tike for all other elements on the page to update. For example, if I have a large dataframe in `data_editor`, is it possible the time the frontend needs to reassemble that into a rerun message potentially greater than 10ms? I don't know how you'd upper-bound that question...

I'm not very familiar with the frontend execution model but i think a delay would only reliably work if it's a "first-in-first-out" situation. I.e. when an element starts processing to emit a rerun request back to the server it aquires some lock which prevents other elements (e.g. button) from starting to process their own. Then a short delay might work in all scenarios because you only need to bound the time required for an element to _enter_ the processing of its rerun request, not the whole thing.
